Estimate regression relationships that vary across latent classes

Source: R/mixture-regression.R
mixture_regression.Rd

mixture_regression() asks whether the relationship between an outcome and its predictors differs across latent classes. The conditional outcome distribution is a mixture of class-specific regressions, so classes can differ in outcome level, in predictor associations or in trajectory over time. Regression parameters and class probabilities are estimated jointly by maximum likelihood.

Predictors in formula describe variation within classes; covariates in membership describe who belongs to which class. A coefficient may be shared by every class (common). Class membership can belong to each row or to every row of a unit (class_level); with a time predictor and shared membership the classes are trajectories, and random adds within-class variation around them (a growth mixture model). Outcomes can be Gaussian, binomial, Poisson, negative binomial or ordinal.

Usage

mixture_regression(
  formula,
  data,
  n_classes,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial", "ordinal"),
  id = NULL,
  class_level = c("observation", "group"),
  n_group_classes = 1L,
  common = NULL,
  membership = ~1,
  group_membership = ~1,
  variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  n_starts = 10L,
  max_iter = 1000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  min_variance = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  missing = c("error", "omit"),
  select_start = c("likelihood", "converged"),
  vcov_type = c("observed", "robust", "opg", "none"),
  weights = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  random_covariance = c("varying", "equal", "proportional"),
  random_diagonal = FALSE,
  cluster = NULL,
  residual_correlation = c("none", "ar", "brownian"),
  residual_time = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula outcome ~ predictors. Factors, interactions and offset() are supported.

data

A data frame.

n_classes

Number of regression classes.

family

"gaussian" (default), "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial" or "ordinal". See Families.

id

NULL (default), or the column identifying the units (persons, schools) the rows belong to.

class_level

"observation" (default): each row has its own class. "group": all rows of a unit share a class (needs id). See Nesting.

n_group_classes

Number of second-level group classes (default 1, none). For class_level = "observation" with id, classes of the units: a unit's class sets the class probabilities of its rows. For a growth mixture with cluster, classes of the clusters.

common

Predictor terms whose coefficients are shared by every class, as names ("age") or a one-sided formula (~ age). Each term must appear in formula; the intercept cannot be shared.

membership

Covariates of class membership, a multinomial logit with the first class as reference: names or a one-sided formula (~ 1, the default, for none). Row-level under "observation", constant within units under "group".

group_membership

Covariates of the group class, as names or a one-sided formula; constant within the units that carry group classes (the id units, or the clusters under cluster).

variance

"varying" (default): a residual standard deviation (or negative-binomial dispersion) per class; "equal": one shared. Gaussian and negative-binomial families only.

n_starts

Number of random starts (default 10), besides one start built from the residuals of a pooled regression. Each start runs up to 50 EM iterations; the better half (at least two) continue to convergence.

max_iter

Maximum EM iterations per start (default 1000).

tol

Convergence tolerance (default 1e-8), per row: EM stops when a step changes the log likelihood by no more than tol times the number of rows of positive weight.

min_variance

Floor on a Gaussian residual variance, as a fraction of the outcome's variance (default 1e-6). A start in which a class's residual variance reaches the floor is excluded from selection. In a growth mixture the same floor bounds each random effect's conditional variance; a random-effect variance at the floor is kept and warned about.

seed

Optional integer seed; when given, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

missing

"error" (default) rejects rows with a missing value in any variable the model uses; "omit" drops them with a warning saying how many.

select_start

"likelihood" (default): the start with the highest likelihood; "converged": the best start that converged.

vcov_type

Covariance of the estimates stored with the fit: "observed" (default, inverse observed information), "robust" (sandwich, clustered on the independent units), "opg" (outer product of the scores) or "none". A weighted fit takes "robust" or "none" only.

weights

Name of a numeric column holding a sampling weight per independent unit (per row without id, per unit with it): pseudo maximum likelihood with robust standard errors. A unit of weight zero is absent from the fit and every criterion but keeps its row and posterior.

random

NULL (default), or the random effects within classes: names such as "time" (a random intercept and a random slope on time) or "intercept", or a one-sided formula such as ~ 1 + time (~ 0 + time for a slope alone). See Growth mixture models.

random_covariance

How the random-effect covariance differs across classes: "varying" (default, one per class), "equal" (one shared matrix, lcmm::hlme(nwg = FALSE)) or "proportional" (a shared matrix times a class-specific scale, the last class's being one, nwg = TRUE).

random_diagonal

TRUE for uncorrelated random effects (idiag = TRUE in lcmm); default FALSE.

cluster

Column grouping the units of id into clusters, such as schools, for the multilevel growth mixture model (with random): each cluster belongs to one of n_group_classes group classes, which sets the trajectory-class probabilities of its persons. The clusters are the independent units of the likelihood, the standard errors and the BIC. See Growth mixture models.

residual_correlation

"none" (default): independent residuals within a unit. With random, "ar" adds a continuous-time autoregressive process (covariance sd^2 * exp(-rate * |t - s|)) and "brownian" Brownian motion (sd^2 * min(t, s)) to the residuals, shared by the classes: lcmm::hlme(cor = AR(time)) and cor = BM(time). A process the data cannot separate from the residual variance or the random effects stays on its bound, warns, and has no standard error. These fits refine one class placement from the model without the process; n_best_replicated is NA, and "starts" reports the correlated fit rather than the initialization's replication count.

residual_time

Numeric time column of the residual process; default the first numeric variable in random, otherwise in the predictors. Brownian motion needs non-negative times.

Value

A latents_mixture_regression object, or latents_growth_mixture when random is given. as.data.frame() returns the coefficient table and get_results() every table by name; predict(), plot() (and plot_trajectories(), plot_coefficients()), summary(), coef(), vcov(), confint(), logLik() and nobs() apply. The within-class coefficients are conditional associations under the specified model, not causal effects; check the starts table and the classification diagnostics before reading substance into the classes.

Nesting

id = NULL

Each row is an independent unit.

class_level = "group"

All rows of a unit share a class, the regression mixture for repeated measures (flexmix(y ~ x | id)); a unit's likelihood is the product of its rows' densities.

class_level = "observation" with id and n_group_classes >= 2

Each row has its own class, and a group class of its unit sets the class probabilities. With n_group_classes = 1, id clusters the robust standard errors and is the unit of weights.

Growth mixture models

With repeated measurements (id, class_level = "group") and time in formula, the classes are trajectories: without random effects a latent class growth model, with random a growth mixture model. For unit i in class k,

$$y_i = X_i \beta_k + Z_i b_i + e_i, \quad b_i \sim N(0, G_k), \quad e_i \sim N(0, \sigma_k^2 I),$$

with Z the design of random. Random effects need the Gaussian family, id, class_level = "group" and, for a random intercept, repeated rows in at least some units. With residual_correlation, e_i also carries the autoregressive or Brownian process over residual_time.

With cluster, persons are nested in clusters and each cluster belongs to a group class h that sets the trajectory-class logits of its persons (a class-specific intercept with shared covariate slopes):

$$L = \prod_j \sum_h \omega_h \prod_{i \in j} \sum_k \pi_{k|h} f_k(y_i)$$

group_membership names cluster-level covariates of the group class; the group classes are in get_results(fit, "group_classes") and "clusters". With n_group_classes = 1 the fit is comparable by BIC with fits that add group classes.

Families

"gaussian": identity link, a residual standard deviation per class or one shared. "binomial": logit link; the outcome is 0/1, logical, a two-level factor (second level the success) or cbind(successes, failures). "poisson": log link, offset() honoured. "negative_binomial": log link, NB2 (variance mu + alpha * mu^2) with a dispersion per class or one shared; a dispersion estimated at zero is the Poisson limit, reported with a warning and no standard error.

"ordinal": a cumulative-logit (proportional-odds) regression within each class, \(P(Y \le c \mid x, k) = \mathrm{plogis}(t_{kc} - x'\beta_k)\), with ordered thresholds per class in place of the intercept and the sign convention of MASS::polr(): a positive slope raises the probability of a higher category. The outcome is an ordered factor, a factor (levels in order) or whole numbers; the categories are those observed, at least two. The formula keeps its intercept, which the thresholds replace. Thresholds appear in the coefficient table as "threshold:<lower>|<upper>", and exp_estimate of a slope is a cumulative odds ratio. The class mean of an ordinal outcome (fitted values, trajectories) is the expected category score with categories scored 1 to C; predict(type = "probabilities") gives the category probabilities.

Identification. Call the thing that carries a class the unit: a row, or an id group under class_level = "group". An ordinal mixture whose units have one outcome each and no predictors is not identified (a mixture of categorical distributions is itself one) and is refused. A binary mixture with one trial per unit, and an ordinal one with one outcome per unit and two categories, are refused too: whether such a model is identified depends on the covariate design, which the package does not assess. Give each unit several outcomes (class_level = "group") or, for binomial, counts with more than one trial per row. A single-level ordinal mixture is also refused when it has more free parameters than the distinct covariate patterns can identify. Repeated binary or ordinal outcomes without predictors must also have enough distinct response-count patterns to identify the class parameters. A growth model is refused when its random-effects and residual covariance components cannot be separated by the observed designs. With class-specific residual variances, two common waves do not identify an unrestricted random intercept and slope covariance. A diagonal covariance can be identified there, as can proportional class covariances with a shared residual variance.

Unused factor levels in membership and random-effects formulas are dropped before fitting. In output tables, an identifier whose name conflicts with a result column is prefixed with id_ or cluster_ (for example, an id = "class" column is returned as id_class, beside the latent class). A numeric suffix is added if that name is also occupied.

Every refusal and warning is a classed condition; latents-conditions lists them.

See also

enumerate_regressions() to compare numbers of classes; plot_trajectories(), plot_coefficients() and, for fits that classify persons, plot_classification().

Examples

fit <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                          n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
fit
#> Mixture of gaussian regressions: 2 classes (one class per row)
#> score ~ hours
#> 900 rows | log likelihood -3144.0073 | BIC 6335.63 | entropy 0.443
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 53 | best likelihood reached by 2 of 2 completed starts (4 run)
#> 
#> Classes
#> 
#> Class    Share  Expected  Rows assigned  Avg. posterior  Residual SD
#> -------  -----  --------  -------------  --------------  -----------
#> Class 1  0.564    507.71            573           0.789         5.24
#> Class 2  0.436    392.29            327           0.829         6.89
#> 
#> Regression coefficients (95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Term       Estimate          95% CI      p
#> -------  ---------  --------  --------------  -----
#> Class 1  Intercept     34.36  [32.95, 35.77]  <.001
#> Class 1  hours          4.57  [ 4.36,  4.77]  <.001
#> Class 2  Intercept     54.90  [52.76, 57.04]  <.001
#> Class 2  hours          0.81  [ 0.48,  1.14]  <.001
#> 
#> Every table: get_results(x, what = ), e.g. "classes", "membership", "fit", "assignments".
as.data.frame(fit)
#> Regression coefficients (95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Term       Estimate          95% CI      p
#> -------  ---------  --------  --------------  -----
#> Class 1  Intercept     34.36  [32.95, 35.77]  <.001
#> Class 1  hours          4.57  [ 4.36,  4.77]  <.001
#> Class 2  Intercept     54.90  [52.76, 57.04]  <.001
#> Class 2  hours          0.81  [ 0.48,  1.14]  <.001
get_results(fit, "classes")
#> Classes
#> 
#> Class    Share  Expected  Rows assigned  Avg. posterior  Residual SD
#> -------  -----  --------  -------------  --------------  -----------
#> Class 1  0.564    507.71            573           0.789         5.24
#> Class 2  0.436    392.29            327           0.829         6.89

# One class per student, several rows per student:
by_student <- mixture_regression(score ~ hours, data = study_hours, n_classes = 2,
                                 id = "student", class_level = "group",
                                 n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
get_results(by_student, "fit")
#> Model fit
#> 
#> Family          gaussian
#> Nesting         group
#> Classes         2
#> Group classes   1
#> Observations    900
#> Groups          150
#> Parameters      7
#> Log likelihood  -3177.76
#> AIC             6369.52
#> BIC             6390.60
#> SABIC           6368.44
#> ICL             6451.31
#> Entropy         0.708
#> Smallest class  46.9%
#> Converged       yes

# \donttest{
# Students nested in schools, each school in one of two group classes:
schools <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, growth_schools, n_classes = 2,
                              id = "student", class_level = "group",
                              random = "wave", random_covariance = "equal",
                              cluster = "school", n_group_classes = 2,
                              n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_results(schools, "group_classes")
#> Group classes: trajectory classes within each
#> 
#> Group class    Class    Probability     SE  Share of clusters  Clusters
#> -------------  -------  -----------  -----  -----------------  --------
#> Group class 1  Class 1        0.842  0.024              0.544        22
#> Group class 1  Class 2        0.158  0.024              0.544        22
#> Group class 2  Class 1        0.233  0.030              0.456        18
#> Group class 2  Class 2        0.767  0.030              0.456        18
